topics.name: Divine hiddenness
topics.description: Schellenberg's hiddenness argument (1993 onward) and the debate it started: whether a perfectly loving God would allow nonresistant nonbelief, plus recent philosophy of religion.

lead.question: Does robust contrastive responsibility for actualising one world rather than another require irreducibly de se content in divine cognition, or can a rigid, de re representation of an agent's controlling intention and its act suffice when the agent's identity is not in doubt?

topics.name: Decision theory in philosophy of religion
topics.description: Decision-theoretic reasoning about God and by God: Newcomb's problem and divine foreknowledge (God as the perfect predictor), Pascal's wager with its infinite utilities and the many-gods objection, and God's own decision problem, whether a perfect being must create the best world, and whether there is one to create.
topics.area: philosophy of religion and decision theory

lead.question: Does diachronic psychological coherence, read as evidence-responsive, disposition-level coherence rather than persistence of every intention, license the backtracking counterfactuals in c004 that tie a token choice in Newcomb's Problem to the predictor's prediction, and if so, does this support one-boxing as the rational choice?

topics.name: Divine simplicity
topics.description: The classical doctrine that God has no parts, properties or composition distinct from God, and the current debate over it: the modal collapse argument, the problem of God's contingent knowledge and free choice, whether God can be identical to a property, truthmaker and constituent-ontology reconstructions, and recent attempts to restate simplicity in new metaphysical terms.
topics.area: philosophy of religion and analytic metaphysics

lead.question: Does a composite, Platonist God face an aseity threat that the simplicity argument uniquely identifies, or is the threat fully explained by the independent existence of the forms, which would leave simplicity idle?
